english.goal: I can find interesting words in a story. I know that prefixes and suffixes change what a word means.

learn.title: Interesting words
learn.text: Writers choose interesting words to make a story exciting. Instead of saying big, a writer might say huge, gigantic or enormous!

learn.title: Words that paint a picture
learn.text: Interesting words help us picture the story in our heads. A tiny bird. A sparkling river. Can you see them?

learn.title: Be a word detective
learn.text: When you find a new word, look for clues in the story and the pictures to work out what it means. Then try using it in your own sentence!

learn.title: Prefixes go at the start
learn.text: A prefix is a small part we add to the START of a word. It changes the meaning. un- means not. re- means again.

learn.title: Suffixes go at the end
learn.text: A suffix is added to the END of a word. -ful means full of. -ly tells us how something is done.

practice.title: Find interesting words
practice.text:
Early one sunny morning, a little dinosaur called Rex woke up in the lush green forest. He stretched his tiny arms and yawned.
Then Rex heard a gigantic splash! He tiptoed past the enormous trees and found a sparkling river. A huge dinosaur with a long neck was drinking the cool water.
Suddenly, a flock of tiny birds zoomed into the sky. "How mysterious!" whispered Rex. He felt curious and brave, so he followed the river to see what he could discover.
practice.prompt: Tap 4 interesting words in the story.
practice.missHint: That's a useful word, but try a more exciting one!

practice.title: Build words
practice.prompt: Make the word with the pieces.

practice.title: Prefix or suffix?
practice.prompt: Is the extra part at the start or the end?

more.title: Word meanings
more.prompt: Match each word to what it means.

items.t: The blue river was ___ in the sun.
He saw a ___ dinosaur with a very long neck.
The birds zoomed away. "How ___!" whispered Rex.

more.title: My own sentence
more.text: Choose your favourite interesting word. Say what it means, then write your own sentence with it.
more.example: Gigantic means very, very big. The gigantic camel walked across the desert.

maths.goal: I can make and break 2-digit numbers using tens and ones, and write number names up to 100.

learn.title: A ten is a stick of 10
learn.text: When we have 10 little ones, we can bundle them into 1 ten. We draw a ten as a long stick.

learn.title: Reading a 2-digit number
learn.text: 34 has 3 tens and 4 ones. The first digit tells us the tens. The second digit tells us the ones.

learn.title: Where a digit sits matters
learn.text: The same digit can be worth different amounts. In 47, the 4 is worth 40. In 74, the 4 is worth just 4!

learn.title: Swap 10 ones for a ten
learn.text: If we have 10 or more ones, we can swap 10 of them for 1 ten. The number stays the same.

learn.title: Number names
learn.text: Say the tens word, then the ones word, with a little dash between. Careful: it's forty, not fourty!
learn.extra: twenty · thirty · forty · fifty · sixty · seventy · eighty · ninety

practice.title: How many blocks?
practice.prompt: Count the tens, then the ones.

practice.prompt: Match each number to its name.

more.prompt: Add sticks and squares to make the number.

science.goal: I know where rocks come from and what we use them for. I can say what a habitat is and match animals to their habitats.

learn.title: Where do rocks come from?
learn.text: We dig rocks out of the ground in quarries and mines, and find them in river beds. Diggers and trucks move them, because rocks are very heavy.

learn.title: What we use rocks for
learn.text: Rocks are strong, so we use them to build things. In the UAE, rocks and sand help build tall towers and long roads.

learn.title: Looking after nature
learn.text: Digging a quarry can remove trees and plants, and take away animals' homes. That's why we should only take the rocks we really need.

learn.title: What is a habitat?
learn.text: A habitat is the place where an animal lives. It gives the animal the food, water and shelter it needs.

learn.title: The Arctic and the desert
learn.text: Animals live in habitats that suit them. The UAE has a desert habitat, where camels and the Arabian oryx live.

practice.title: Who lives where?
practice.prompt: Match each animal to its habitat.

practice.title: Arctic or desert?
practice.prompt: Which habitat does each word describe?

opts: Trees and plants may be removed

more.title: Rock scratch test
more.text: Find 3 different stones. With a grown-up, try to scratch each one with a paperclip. Which stone is hard? Which is soft?
steps: Look at each stone. Is it big or small?
Scratch it gently with the paperclip.
If it scratches easily, it is soft. If not, it is hard!

more.title: Why does it live there?
more.text: Choose an animal. Tell a grown-up: "It lives in the ___ because ___." Try to give two clues about its habitat.
more.example: A camel lives in the desert because it can go a long time without water, and its wide feet don't sink in the sand.

gp.goal: I can name the seven continents and find them on a world map.

learn.title: What is a continent?
learn.text: The biggest pieces of land on Earth are called continents. There are 7 of them!

learn.title: Island, country, continent
learn.text: An island is small. A country is bigger. A continent is the biggest of all, and has many countries in it.

learn.title: Where do we live?
learn.text: We live in the UAE. The UAE is a country in Asia. Asia is the biggest continent in the world!

learn.title: Biggest to smallest
learn.text: Asia is the biggest continent. Australia is the smallest. Antarctica is covered in ice, and penguins live there.
learn.big: Asia · Africa · North America · South America · Antarctica · Europe · Australia

opts: A very large area of land

items.q: We live in the UAE. Which continent is that?

practice.prompt: Tap the continents from biggest to smallest.

more.title: Where would you go?
more.text: Which continent would you like to visit, and why? Tell your family one animal or place you would love to see there.

msc.goal: I can name people who are important to me and show care and kindness to them.

learn.title: Important people
learn.text: Our family and friends care for us, keep us safe and make us happy. Teachers help us learn.

learn.title: Showing care
learn.text: We show care with kind words and kind actions: helping, sharing, and saying please and thank you.

learn.title: Kind or unkind?
learn.text: Helping a friend who falls is kind. Laughing at them is unkind. Before we act, we can ask: will this make someone feel good?

items.t: Helping a friend pick up their pencils
Leaving someone out of a game

items.q: Your friend drops her crayons. What is kind?
Grandma looks tired. What could you do?

opts: Please may I have a turn?
